summary: Reconciled CORE-001 into a frontend-only enterprise product experience spanning public entry, persistent staff operations, patient and caregiver portals, and one fully deterministic Maria treatment-readiness journey.
decisions: Implement CORE-001 as one React + TypeScript + Vite browser application with public entry, sandbox role/session entry, a persistent staff shell, and focused patient and caregiver portal contexts.

The staff shell must navigate to Command Center, Exceptions, Patients/case workspace, Resources, Insights, Integrations, and Admin; only the Maria path and demo-critical shared state require full transactional behavior.

Use typed synthetic enterprise fixtures for secondary patients, cases, resources, sites, metrics, integrations, and configuration, while a deterministic reducer or equivalent state machine owns Maria's workflow, permissions, persistence, and reset.

Use one workflow-event source of truth to derive Maria's queue/case state, Treatment Readiness Graph, timeline, command-center signal, patient status, and caregiver projection so the cross-surface demonstration cannot drift.

Make public calls to action, sandbox entry, primary staff navigation, patient/exception search and filters, the Maria golden path, the caregiver privacy filter, guarded routing, recovery, and reset functional; secondary enterprise content may be static/read-only when clearly represented.

Keep routing deterministic: one readiness submission creates separate clinical-review and transportation-navigation tasks, and treatment confirmation requires appropriate staff action plus Maria's acknowledgment.
Treat clinical and search text as untrusted inert content; no AI or client heuristic may make a clinical decision, downgrade urgency, clear treatment, or control workflow safety.
Enforce Ana's caregiver experience through an allowlisted data projection that excludes clinical concern and task details from visible, indexed, and accessibility-specific caregiver output.

Represent sign-in as local sandbox/session entry rather than authentication, and represent integrations, operational data, resources, configuration, protocols, and outcomes as synthetic, sandbox, simulated, proposed, or read-only where material.
Do not claim production deployment, live Ochsner/vendor connectivity, security/compliance certification, clinical validation, production-scale authorization, or measured outcomes.
Use versioned browser persistence with safe fallback and a broadly available one-click reset to protect the deadline-critical demonstration.
Keep the task contract-free because all behavior remains inside one frontend implementation with no live external or independently implemented component boundary.

risks.description: The expanded enterprise surface area could consume the deadline while weakening the only end-to-end proof judges need.
risks.mitigation: Implement the shared shell, navigation, fixtures, and Maria state model first; make secondary modules complete but static/read-only and stop adding depth once acceptance-critical navigation, search/filter, privacy, and golden-path behavior pass.

risks.description: Fixture-driven enterprise screens and independently presented metrics could contradict Maria's workflow and make the product feel staged.
risks.mitigation: Derive all Maria and current-treatment signals from one workflow/event source and keep unrelated historical metrics explicitly synthetic and stable.

risks.description: Sign-in, Integrations, Admin, Trust, or resource screens could imply real authentication, production policy enforcement, vendor connectivity, compliance, certification, or fulfillment.
risks.mitigation: Use local sandbox entry without real credentials, label material synthetic/sandbox/proposed states, remove unsupported badges or status claims, and render nonfunctional consequential controls read-only, disabled with a reason, or absent.

risks.description: Caregiver projection or shared search/index fixtures could expose Maria's synthetic clinical concern outside the patient/staff context.
risks.mitigation: Build caregiver data from an explicit transportation-only allowlist and assert that clinical data is absent from rendered, accessibility, and caregiver-specific searchable output.

risks.description: The wider route and local-state surface could make reset or refresh return different modules to contradictory states during the live demonstration.
risks.mitigation: Version persisted state, centralize initialization/reset, clear relevant navigation/search/filter/session state, and exercise public-entry-to-confirmed plus reset in the smoke check.

risks.description: Broad synthetic datasets can create broken search/filter combinations or empty screens that appear unfinished.
risks.mitigation: Keep fixture volume small and coherent, implement predictable combination and clear-filter behavior, and design explicit no-result/unknown states.

notes_for_next_agent: The human-approved scope now includes public landing/sign-in/trust, seven persistent staff modules, and patient/caregiver portals; the previous five-screen-only and no-marketing constraints no longer apply.

Because the approved architecture scope changed after earlier design evidence, Gemini design evidence and compatibility approval must be refreshed and bound to this exact expanded scope before Phase B production implementation.
Build in this order: route/shell and fixtures, Maria state/permissions/reset, public and portal entry, primary search/filters, golden path, then static enterprise breadth and polish.

Maria is the only required fully interactive patient. Secondary patients, metrics, resources, integrations, and Admin may be stable synthetic/read-only content when their navigation and states are complete and truthful.
Internal TypeScript types and fixture schemas are not a formal contract. Do not invent endpoints or implement against the repository's empty OpenAPI placeholder.

Make caregiver clinical-data exclusion, inert free-text rendering, sandbox sign-in truthfulness, integration/admin claim restraint, guarded transitions, reset, and reduced-motion equivalence acceptance-critical.

SMOKE depth remains implementation-owned: cover public/workspace entry, route reachability, search/filter recovery, the deterministic Maria flow, caregiver exclusion, and reset; no independent tester or dedicated security reviewer is selected.
